Senior DevOps / SRE Engineer, Long-Term, On-Call & Production Ownership
Posted 4 minutes ago
Worldwide

Summary
We are a growing company looking for a senior DevOps / SRE engineer to become a long-term part of our small technical team.

We’re a relatively small company, which means you’ll have a lot of ownership and very little bureaucracy. You’ll work directly with the founder and our developers, make your own recommendations, and have the freedom to improve how we run production.

We’re looking for someone we can trust and call when something goes wrong, but just as importantly, someone who proactively makes sure those calls become less frequent over time.

The environment

Our stack includes:

* DigitalOcean
* Cloudflare
* Linux / Nginx
* WordPress + WooCommerce
* Laravel + Vue
* MySQL
* GitHub
* Payment integrations
* APIs between several internal and external systems
* ERP and third-party logistics integrations

We’re actively developing our platform, so there will be plenty of opportunities to improve how things are built, monitored and operated.

What you’ll own

We want someone who can take responsibility for areas such as:

* Production monitoring, logging and alerting
* Incident response and root-cause analysis
* Server and application performance
* Cloudflare, networking, DNS and DDoS protection
* Security hardening
* Secrets, credentials and access management
* Backups and disaster recovery
* CI/CD and safer deployments
* Identifying risks before they become incidents
* Debugging across infrastructure and application layers
* Runbooks and documentation

We care more about outcomes than rigid role boundaries.

For example, if customers successfully place orders but those orders stop syncing between WooCommerce and our Laravel application, we don’t want to hear “the server is running, ask the developer.”

We want you to investigate the problem, work with the developer if needed, find the root cause, get production healthy again and make sure we’ll detect the problem automatically next time.

Who we’re looking for

You have significant experience running real production systems and are comfortable taking ownership when things go wrong.

You are:

* Excellent at debugging
* Experienced with production incidents and on-call work
* Strong on monitoring and observability
* Security-minded
* Proactive rather than reactive
* Comfortable going beyond infrastructure when necessary
* Good at communicating technical problems simply
* Calm and structured during incidents
* Interested in the business impact, not just the technology
* Someone who prefers simple, reliable systems over unnecessary complexity

Experience with DigitalOcean, Cloudflare, WooCommerce and/or Laravel is a strong plus.

Why this could be a great fit

We’re not looking for someone to disappear into a large engineering organization.

You’ll work with a small team where your decisions have a visible impact. You’ll have direct access to the people making decisions, freedom to suggest and implement improvements, and the opportunity to shape our DevOps/SRE setup rather than inherit years of corporate processes.

We move quickly, experiment a lot and increasingly use AI throughout the company and our development workflows. We’re looking for someone who enjoys that kind of environment.

Engagement

We’re looking for a long-term relationship, not a one-off project.

Initially, we expect around 10-20 hours per month, plus availability for urgent production incidents.

We’re building a small group of trusted DevOps/SRE engineers so nobody needs to personally cover 24/7.

Insurance Workflow automation for Financial advice SaaS
Posted 12 minutes ago
Worldwide

Summary
Build an end-to-end insurance workflow automation feature for a multi-tenant financial advice SaaS platform, replacing a manual process where advisers prepared client insurance information and emailed it to multiple insurers.

The solution brings the complete outbound workflow into the existing SaaS platform while keeping insurers on the email systems they already use. It combines structured data collection, insurance needs analysis, document generation, transactional email, delivery tracking, and auditability into a single workflow.

Key deliverables include:

• Client insurance pre-assessment forms with per-person submissions and mandatory adviser review
• Automated insurance needs summaries combining calculator data and existing policy information
• Branded, white-labelled A4 PDF generation using headless Chromium, including de-identified versions for privacy-sensitive workflows
• Multi-tenant insurer configuration with dealer group → practice → adviser settings inheritance and per-send overrides
• Email composition with attachments, scanned-file validation, configurable recipients, and exact per-recipient previews
• Serverless email dispatch through Amazon SES with one individually addressed email per insurer and idempotent send protection
• SES/SNS-based delivery, bounce and complaint tracking with recipient-level status and retry handling
• Immutable enquiry snapshots and a complete audit trail of what was sent, to whom, when, and by whom
• Consent gates and privacy controls designed around the handling of sensitive insurance and health information

The feature is designed for integration into an existing production SaaS codebase rather than as an isolated application, with integration across existing forms, client records, document storage, authentication, email infrastructure, and AWS serverless services.

Tech stack: React, Node.js, Material UI, Redux, AWS Amplify, AWS AppSync, GraphQL, AWS Lambda, DynamoDB, Amazon SES, Amazon SNS, Amazon S3, Amazon Cognito, and Puppeteer/headless Chromium.

Production-Grade Full-Stack Engineer Needed for Existing Video Collaboration Platform
Posted 3 hours ago
Worldwide

Summary
Senior Full-Stack Engineer Needed for 2-Day Production Readiness Sprint

Fixed budget: $60 total
Duration: 2 days

I have already built a video collaboration platform similar to Frame.io. I am looking for an experienced full-stack engineer to spend 2 focused days reviewing the existing application and bringing the core software to a production-grade standard.

This is not a greenfield project and I am not looking for someone to rebuild the product.

The software already exists. I need someone who can quickly understand the existing codebase, identify the important production risks, and fix them.

What I have built

The platform is a video collaboration and review platform with functionality similar to Frame.io, including:

Video projects
Folders and project organisation
Video uploads
Video playback
Video asset management
Time-based comments on videos
Replies to comments
Resolving comments
Video review workflows
Video versions
Project collaboration
User permissions
Client-facing project views
Media previews
Project activity and collaboration
Google Workspace integration

The key difference is that the platform connects to a client's Google account.

The intended workflow is:

Gmail + Google Drive → Our Platform → Video Review → Comments → Collaboration

Video projects may be delivered through Google Drive and discussed through Gmail.

The platform is designed to automatically identify relevant project information from Gmail and Google Drive and bring it into the appropriate project.

This means users can work from one central platform rather than manually moving information between Gmail, Drive and the video collaboration system.

Your 2-day task

Your job is to take the existing application through a focused production-readiness pass.

Day 1: Audit and critical issues

Understand the architecture and test the main workflows.

Focus on:

Authentication
User permissions
Project permissions
Client/tenant isolation
Video upload and playback
Comments and replies
Video versions
Project workflows
Gmail integration
Google Drive integration
OAuth
Data syncing
Error handling
Background processes
API failures
Duplicate data
Obvious performance problems

Identify anything that could cause a real client to experience a broken workflow, incorrect data, security issue or unreliable behaviour.

Day 2: Fix and harden

Prioritise the most important issues discovered during the audit and fix them.

This may include:

Broken workflows
Authentication issues
Permission issues
Data isolation problems
Google integration issues
Sync problems
Duplicate processing
Error handling
Retry behaviour
UI/backend inconsistencies
Obvious performance issues
Other critical production bugs

The goal is to leave the application in a meaningfully more reliable state after the two days.

What "production-grade" means

I am not looking for someone to simply test the happy path and say that everything works.

Think about what happens when:

A Google token expires
A Gmail or Drive API request fails
A webhook is missed
The same email or file is processed twice
A background job fails
A user refreshes during an operation
Two users perform an action at the same time
A user does not have access to a Drive file
A project contains a large amount of data
A client reconnects their Google account

The software needs to handle real-world conditions properly.

We have deadlines and need to work efficiently. Working efficiently does not mean cutting corners.

Important

You will be working with an existing codebase, so you need to be able to understand unfamiliar software quickly.

I am specifically looking for someone who can think independently and identify problems without needing every issue handed to them.

I do not want someone who only says:

"This feature works."

I want someone who asks:

"What happens when this fails?"

Required experience

Experience with:

Full-stack SaaS
Google OAuth
Gmail API
Google Drive API
REST APIs
Databases
Authentication and authorisation
Multi-tenant applications
Background jobs
Webhooks
Production debugging
Automated testing

Experience with video collaboration software or products similar to Frame.io is a plus.

Deliverable after 2 days

At the end of the engagement, I expect:

The critical workflows tested.
Production risks identified.
The highest-priority issues fixed.
Any remaining issues clearly documented.
A short explanation of what was changed and why.

Duration: 2 days
Budget: $60 fixed

Please only apply if you are comfortable working within this scope and can start quickly.

To apply

What is your experience taking existing software and making it production-ready?
Have you worked with Gmail API and Google Drive API?
Have you worked with multi-tenant SaaS?
What would you check first when given an existing application like this?

description: A B2B SaaS company with a small engineering team and 5-6 production applications wants a senior engineer for 6-9 months to build an AI-agent-driven software delivery pipeline: automated spec intake from Jira, risk-based gating, unattended agent build sessions producing tested PRs, AI code review with auto-merge rules, security scanning, and OpenTelemetry-based production monitoring.
raw_input:
Senior AI-native Engineer: Help us build our Software Delivery Pipeline
Posted 38 minutes ago
Worldwide

Summary
## Description

We are a B2B SaaS company with a small engineering team, five to six production applications, and a growing enterprise customer base. We want to ship 3-5x more with the same team by putting AI agents to work across the whole software delivery process, not just in the editor and certainly not "vibes".

We are hiring one senior engineer for 6-9 months to help build that system with us. You will work with the Director of Engineering and our senior developers.

**What you will build**

- **Spec intake.** We already have an internal agent workspace that rewrites Jira cards into specs grounded in our actual code. Today it runs by hand, one card at a time. You will make it run daily on new cards and customer bug reports, and make it usable by product managers.
- **Risk gates.** Rate each change by risk (database migrations, auth, tenant data, cross-app contracts, test coverage). Low-risk work goes straight to an agent. High-risk work goes to a senior developer first.
- **Agent builds.** Agent sessions that take a spec and open a tested pull request.
- **Automated code review and merge rules.** Set up and tune an AI code review platform. Low-risk PRs auto-merge to staging for manual QA; high-risk PRs get human review before trunk.
- **Security scanning.** Dependency, code, and secret scanning on every PR, plus scheduled scans of production.
- **Production watch.** OpenTelemetry across all applications, and an agent that watches for errors, slow queries, and regressions after each deploy.

**Must have**

1. **Extensive hands-on experience with AI coding tools:** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or similar. You use them daily, you know where each one fails, and you have run them unattended, not only in chat.
2. **Experience setting up and managing AI code review platforms:** CodeRabbit, Graphite, or similar. You have tuned rules and cut noise so developers trust the output.
3. **Experience building both agent skills and deterministic workflows.** Skills, custom commands, subagents, or MCP servers on the agent side. Pipelines, scheduled jobs, and CI on the deterministic side. You know when a step needs a model and when it needs plain code.
4. CI/CD on GitHub Actions: branch protection, required checks, staging deploys.
5. PostgreSQL and data pipelines in production.
6. Observability with OpenTelemetry or a similar standard.
7. Security scanning tools (SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, DAST).
8. Clear written and spoken English. Most of the work can be asynchronous, but regular meetings on Zoom with Dir of Eng and other developers would be part of the weekly cadence.

**Strong pluses**

- Kestra or another workflow orchestrator (Airflow, Temporal, Prefect)
- .NET and Azure (App Services, Functions)
- TypeScript or Python
- Load testing (k6, JMeter, or similar)
- Feature flags and dark launches (PostHog or similar)
- Jira API and automation
- Work in a SOC2 or ISO 27001 environment

**Engagement**

- Full-time (40 hours/week), initial 3 months with a potential to extend to 6-9 months, with a review at the end of each quarter.
- Remote. You need at least 4 hours of overlap with UK and US Eastern business hours.
- Everything you build lives in our repos, with runbooks, so our team can run it after the engagement ends. Handover is part of the job.

**How to apply**

Start your proposal with the word **"SDLC"** so we know you read this. Then, in plain text:

1. Describe one AI agent workflow you built that runs without a person driving it. What triggered it, what it produced, and how you checked the output.
2. Which AI coding tool do you use most, and what is one thing it does badly?
3. Link to code, a repo, a write-up, or a short video of something you built with agents. Private work is fine to describe instead.

Proposals that do not answer these questions will not be reviewed.
